articles.title: Carney promises Arctic investment will benefit Inuit during meeting with leadership
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Inuit leadership in Kuujjuaq, Quebec to discuss Arctic defence and infrastructure investments, marking the first sitting prime minister visit in nearly 20 years.

articles.title: North Coast oil tanker ban being upheld, Port of Vancouver expanding in multibillion-dollar B.C.-Ottawa deal
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and B.C. Premier David Eby announced a Canada-British Columbia Cooperative Prosperity Agreement with $10 billion for Port of Vancouver upgrades and commitment to maintain the North Coast oil tanker ban.

articles.title: Carney announces $200M for new school, updated health centre in Tumbler Ridge
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced $200 million in joint federal-provincial funding for a new secondary school and updated health centre in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

articles.title: As Canadians face high food prices, Carney lays out $3B plan to boost local, affordable access
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled a $3.2 billion food security strategy over a decade to increase domestic food production and affordability, including investments in food terminals and crackdowns on surveillance pricing.

articles.title: Carney announces new sanctions against Russia following G7 meeting with Zelenskyy
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced new sanctions against Russia during the G7 summit in France and met with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy to discuss continued support for Ukraine.
